title: Tunable Ultrastrong Magnon-Magnon Coupling and Squeezed States in a Triaxial Van der Waals Antiferromagnet
authors: Xiao Xiao, Zishuang Li, Zui Tao, Lina Chen, Ping Liu, Shuai Zhang, Haozhe Wang, Yong Pu, Ronghua Liu
abstract: Achieving and quantifying ultrastrong magnon-magnon coupling (USC) remains a key challenge for quantum magnonics. Here, we demonstrate widely tunable USC between chiral (right- and left-handed) and acoustic or optical magnon modes in the van der Waals antiferromagnet $CrPS_4$. Using a full quantum model, we decompose the interaction into three microscopic interaction channels: the co-rotating term $g_1$ (mode hybridization), the counter-rotating term $g_2$ (two-mode squeezing), and, uniquely in the chiral regime, the self-squared term $g_3$ that mediates single-mode squeezing. The normalized coupling ratio reaches $g/f_g$ $\sim$ 0.41, entering the USC regime. Most significantly, we establish a complete protocol linking these USC parameters to a measurable quantum phenomenon: a squeezed magnon vacuum state. Our simulations not only visualize the chirality and polarization evolution of the hybrid modes but also demonstrate how to directly extract quadrature fluctuations and a substantial squeezing factor (up to $\sim$ 9.7 dB) from thermal noise-driven magnetization dynamics. This work provides a material-specific quantum framework for USC and a practical pathway to detect and exploit non-classical magnon states in low-damping two-dimensional magnets, opening a route toward quantum-enhanced spintronics and hybrid quantum information platforms.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of ultrastrong magnon-magnon coupling in the antiferromagnet $	ext{CrPS}_4$ by developing a quantum model that extends beyond the standard approximations. The authors successfully link the microscopic coupling parameters to the macroscopic, measurable quantum phenomenon of magnon squeezing. This establishes a practical quantum framework for utilizing magnons in advanced spintronic and quantum information applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve and quantify ultrastrong magnon-magnon coupling (USC) in a magnetic insulator and link this coupling to the generation of measurable non-classical quantum states, specifically squeezed magnon vacuum states.
main_result: The authors successfully developed a quantum model beyond the Rotating-Wave Approximation to quantify three distinct coupling channels ($g_1, g_2, g_3$) and demonstrated a protocol to extract a substantial squeezing factor (up to $\sim 9.7 	ext{ dB}$) from thermal noise-driven dynamics.
method: The study combines advanced quantum Hamiltonian modeling (going beyond RWA) with both micromagnetic simulations and analysis of experimental Antiferromagnetic Resonance (AFMR) spectroscopy data.
model_or_system: The physical system is the van der Waals antiferromagnet $	ext{CrPS}_4$. The theoretical framework involves a quantum Hamiltonian decomposed into pure and coupling terms, which is analyzed in different coupling regimes (AM-OM and RM-LM).
key_observables: Squeezing factor ($	ext{dB}$), quadrature fluctuations ($\langle\Delta \hat{X}_{\varphi,\psi}^2angle$), coupling strengths ($g_1, g_2, g_3$), and magnon dispersion relations.
important_parameters: Normalized coupling ratio $g/f_g \sim 0.41$, and the USC regime itself.
main_assumptions: The necessity of moving beyond the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) is a key point, as the classical LL model is insufficient for the full quantum description.
figures_summary: Figures show experimental AFMR spectra ($	ext{dP/dH}$) compared to theoretical dispersions, illustrating mode hybridization and the field dependence of the extracted coupling strengths ($g_1, g_2, g_3$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the challenge (USC) to developing a comprehensive quantum model (Hamiltonian decomposition), linking this model to measurable quantum diagnostics (squeezing via quadrature operators), and finally validating the results using both simulation and experimental spectroscopy.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a concrete, material-specific pathway to observe and exploit non-classical quantum states (squeezing) using magnons, bridging condensed matter magnetism with quantum optics principles.
